methods-mc-mi.Rmd
library(package = semmcci)
library(package = lavaan)

Data 

summary(object = df)
#>        X                   M                  Y           
#>  Min.   :-3.199558   Min.   :-3.37128   Min.   :-3.61432  
#>  1st Qu.:-0.632676   1st Qu.:-0.70516   1st Qu.:-0.66921  
#>  Median : 0.028235   Median : 0.02825   Median :-0.04833  
#>  Mean   : 0.002688   Mean   :-0.01992   Mean   :-0.01538  
#>  3rd Qu.: 0.657543   3rd Qu.: 0.65240   3rd Qu.: 0.65293  
#>  Max.   : 3.470910   Max.   : 2.93497   Max.   : 3.09950  
#>  NAs    :100         NAs    :100        NAs    :100

Multiple Imputation

Perform the appropriate multiple imputation approach to deal with missing values. In this example, we impute multivariate missing data under the normal model.

mi <- mice::mice(
  data = df,
  method = "norm",
  m = 100,
  print = FALSE,
  seed = 42
)

Model Specification 

model <- "
  Y ~ cp * X + b * M
  M ~ a * X
  X ~~ X
  indirect := a * b
  direct := cp
  total := cp + (a * b)
"

Model Fitting 

fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model)

Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals 

unstd <- MCMI(lav = fit, mi = mi, R = 20000L, alpha = 0.05)

Methods

print 

print(x = unstd)

Standardized Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals 

fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model, fixed.x = FALSE)
unstd <- MCMI(lav = fit, mi = mi, R = 20000L, alpha = 0.05)
std <- MCStd(mc = unstd, alpha = 0.05)

Methods

print
